parsed.main_gap: Graph argument falsely asserts every component is a tree (q vertices, q-1 edges permits cycles); the component actually used is chosen arbitrarily ('containing a_q'), not shown loop/cycle-free.

errors.description: Edge-count argument is invalid: a graph on q vertices with q-1 edges can contain cycles/loops (e.g. triangle plus isolated vertices). What is true, and all that is needed, is that SOME component satisfies e_C = v_C - 1 and is a tree; the write-up instead claims all components are trees and then picks an arbitrary component, which may have a loop (breaking the ±(x_{2j-1}-x_{2j}) contribution) or an odd cycle (no bipartition).
errors.quote: Having fewer edges than vertices, the graph contains no cycle and no loop, since a cycle or a loop on \(v\) vertices already uses at least \(v\) edges; hence every connected component \(C\) has \(e_C=v_C-1\) and is a tree

errors.description: In (3) the left side involves only edges of the chosen component, while the right side is written as the full sum over all pairs; the inequality is correct (terms are nonnegative) but the write-up does not flag the restriction, and the isolated-vertex case (a_i = x_r) is only alluded to, not verified.
The key cancellation identity in the drafting lemma is asserted rather than derived ('Direct cancellation gives'); routine but unverified in the text.

parsed.notes: Answer 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) is consistent with n=1,2 checks; drafting lemma, refinement upper bound (overlay construction with ≤ q-1 cuts), pigeonhole on 2^{n+1} subset sums, and the geometric construction are all correct. Only the tree-component step is flawed but one-line repairable.
